THIS MIGHT BE ONE OF THE MOST INSANE AI PROJECTS ON GITHUB RIGHT NOW.

121,000 stars. An entire AI-powered trading firm, open-sourced for anyone to explore.

And the crazy part? Every role is handled by an AI agent.

Analysts. Researchers. Traders. Risk managers. Portfolio managers.

Here's what's inside:

«4 analyst agents covering fundamentals, sentiment, news, and technicals.

Bull and bear agents that debate every potential trade before a decision is made.

A trader agent that determines when to enter and how much to allocate.

A 3-agent risk team with aggressive, neutral, and conservative strategies.

A portfolio manager that reviews, approves, or rejects every order.

Support for Claude, GPT, Gemini, Grok, DeepSeek, and local models.

Built-in backtesting to evaluate strategies against historical data.»

Want to turn it into your own AI trading system? Here's the workflow:

1. Clone the repository and open it in Claude Code.

2. Ask Opus 5.5 to explain every agent in plain English so you understand how decisions are made.

3. Choose your models and configure your API keys. Use stronger models for critical decisions and cheaper ones for less demanding tasks.

4. Start with one ticker you understand. Read the full bull-versus-bear debate before trusting any output.

5. Run the built-in backtest over the last 3 years, including realistic fees and slippage. If it can't outperform buy-and-hold after costs, investigate before going further.

6. Explore broker integration, such as Alpaca for stocks or Binance for crypto.

7. Add strict safeguards: fixed position sizing, stop-loss rules, daily loss limits, and an emergency kill switch.

8. Run it in paper-trading mode for at least two weeks. Compare its performance with the backtest.

9. Connect Telegram for decision alerts. Only consider live trading after thorough testing, starting with an amount you can afford to lose.

One important reminder: an impressive AI trading architecture doesn't guarantee profitable trades. Test every strategy and never hand over your capital blindly.

Save this. You'll want to explore it.

items.summary: I understand the appeal. College is busy. Between classes, jobs, extracurriculars, leadership positions and trying to maintain some semblance of a social life, there are never enough hours in the day. AI makes things easier. [...] There is also something to be said about individuality. AI can generate an argument, imitate a writing style or suggest a creative direction, but our perspectives are developed through our own experiences, disagreements, mistakes and interpretations. The things that make our voices interesting are often the very things that cannot be neatly generated from a prompt. If we constantly rely on the same tools to tell us what to think and how to express it, we risk losing the differences that make [...] I am not asking anyone to abandon AI. I use it, and I recognize the benefits it provides. But I do think we need to become more conscientious about when we use it and what we are asking it to do for us. Let it help with the tedious tasks. Let it serve as a resource. But do not let it become a substitute for your own intellectual development.

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là một hàm mà khi lấy đạo hàm sẽ cho ra \( x^2 \). Để tìm nguyên hàm, ta sử dụng công thức:

\[
\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C
\]

Trong trường hợp này, \( n = 2 \):

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^{2+1}}{2+1} + C = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Vậy nguyên hàm của \( x^2 \) là:

\[
\frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đó \( C \) là hằng số tích phân.

items.title: Recent advances in AI are creating a 'paradigm shift' for robotics - Berkeley News
items.summary: Traditionally, engineers can directly program the software that tells robots how to perceive objects, plan movements and control their actions, a process called model-based robotics. Or, with model-free robotics, they can train robots to learn behaviors from demonstrations through imitation learning. The first approach requires extensive engineering, while the second needs enormous amounts of data and time. [...] “Robots are advancing quickly, but developing them for real-world environments remains slow, data-intensive and difficult to scale,” Huang said. “Working with UC Berkeley, NVIDIA is helping advance a new approach combining agentic AI, simulation and open industrial task-focused benchmarks to help developers rapidly test and improve robot behavior before deployment.” [...] Earlier this year, he and his team began experimenting with a change to the way the robot code is organized. Using a framework they called Graph-as-Policy, robot tasks are segmented into individual skills, such as finding an object, planning a grasp and moving the gripper without collisions. Goldberg likened it to individual building blocks that fit together into something much larger.

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] The artificial intelligence company said in its commitments that for data centers it owns and operates, it will solicit community input, publish construction plans and stay away from use of non-disclosure agreements with public officials. Additionally, in a policy blueprint, OpenAI encouraged policymakers to enact similar commitments as laws. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.

items.title: OpenAI employees warned about operational security lapses for years, sources say | Reuters
items.summary:
Even before OpenAI launched ChatGPT in late 2022, some company staffers raised concerns internally about its security practices, according to five people familiar with the matter. Employees shared their concerns with top OpenAI leaders ​and the board of directors, the people said, adding that some staffers came away from those interactions concluding that management was more focused on keeping pace with competitors like Google and Anthropic than on security. [...] Another issue is that OpenAI had not done regular security reviews of its internal tools, such as the so-called sandboxes where researchers stress-test new models, three people familiar with the company’s practices said. Employees often modified those tools for their work, but those changes were not always tested for security problems, leaving them potentially vulnerable to attacks from outsiders, the three people said. [...] OpenAI and Anthropic have tried to ​maintain a more open research culture to both ⁠attract employees and foster creativity that can lead to breakthroughs. The AI field is rooted in academia, where machine-learning scientists have openly discussed their research.

Some OpenAI employees are increasingly worried about this approach as AI grows more capable, according to the five people.
